title: New York Federal Reserve Study:  U S  Consumers and Companies Paid 90% of the 2025 Tariff Taxes
summary: Investor blog video (Feb 2026): a NY Fed study found US firms and consumers paid 90 percent of the 2025 tariffs; pass-through was delayed by stockpiling, gradual pricing and court uncertainty; Brazil tariffs hit beef and coffee.

assertions.quote: US companies and consumers paid 90% of the increase in the Republican tariff taxes imposed by Trump during his second term.
Moran may be the only economist in the world who actually believes that nonsense.
Besset claims that the tariffs are not inflationary, but he stated in early 2024 before he became Treasury Secretary that tariffs were inflationary.
US importers loaded up on the on more far more foreign products than they needed in advance of Trump uh taxing them.

verdicts.note: US imports surged to a record in early 2025 as firms front-ran announced tariffs, and inventories were run down through the year.

assertions.quote: major companies will only gradually increase consumer prices to recoup the Republican tariff taxes paid by them

verdicts.note: Import prices rise almost one for one in the first month, so importers pay the tariff immediately, while retail pass-through of the direct effect is only about half complete after three months and full after six, and the indirect effect via domestic producers keeps building to twelve months.

In May 2026 regional business surveys, 47 percent of tariff-paying service firms and 44 percent of manufacturers said they still had tariff-induced price increases to come, more than a year after the tariffs began, consistent with gradual pass-through after initial absorption.

assertions.quote: coffee was up 18.3% both due to the Republican tariff taxes.

verdicts.note: The 50 percent Brazil tariff added to coffee and beef costs, but coffee was already up sharply on Brazilian drought and beef on a cyclically small US cattle herd and import restrictions.

assertions.quote: The US dollar has lost about 10% of its value against a basket of foreign currencies during Trump's second term.

verdicts.note: The dollar fell about 10 percent in 2025 after the tariffs rather than appreciating, and in 2018-2019 the exchange-rate offset was small.

The dollar depreciated about 2 percent around the Liberation Day announcement rather than appreciating, and adding the exchange rate to the import-price regression leaves tariff pass-through at about 90 percent, so no exchange-rate offset is found.

assertions.quote: no homeowner actually pays rent to themselves.

verdicts.note: OER is imputed rather than paid in cash, but it is the standard way to measure the consumption value of owner-occupied housing and tracks market rents with a lag.
